title: 4 Ingredient Chicken Enchilada Casserole
ingredients: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 2 large)
Chopped green onions or cilantro, for garnish (optional)
steps: Cut each chicken breast into about 3 pieces. Put them in a small pot, pour the enchilada sauce over, cover, and cook on low to medium about 20 minutes until cooked through. No water needed. Stir now and then so it does not stick.
Remove the chicken and shred it with two forks. Heat the oven to 375°F.
Spread about 1/4 cup of the leftover sauce over the bottom of an 8x8-inch dish.
Layer 2 tortillas (halve them to fit), a third of the chicken, a third of the remaining sauce, and a third of the cheese. Repeat twice more for 3 layers.
Bake uncovered 20 to 30 minutes, until bubbly and the cheese is melted and browning in spots.
Rest a few minutes, garnish if you like, and serve warm.
notes: Serves 4. Prep 15 min, cook 45 min. Rotisserie chicken (about 3 to 4 cups shredded) works too: warm it in the sauce, then layer. Make ahead: assemble, cover and refrigerate up to 24 hours (add a few minutes to the bake). Freeze before baking, then bake from frozen at 375°F for 45 to 50 minutes, covered for the first 30. Fridge leftovers keep up to 3 days. Pick a thick, flavorful enchilada sauce since it is most of the flavor.

title: 5 Minute Nacho Cheese Sauce
steps: Whisk the butter and flour in a small pot over medium heat until bubbly and foamy, then keep whisking for about 60 seconds without letting it brown.
Whisk in the milk, turn the heat up slightly, and bring to a simmer, whisking, until thick enough to coat a spoon. Turn off the heat.
Stir in the cheddar one handful at a time until melted. Put it back over low heat if needed to help it melt, but don't overheat.
Stir in the salt and chili powder, taste, and adjust. Add a splash of milk if it's too thick.
notes: Makes about 6 servings of 1/4 cup. Use medium cheddar (sharp can go grainy) and shred it from a block. Best eaten fresh; leftovers keep 3 to 4 days, reheat low and slow with a splash of milk. Mild on purpose, so add jalapeno brine, Rotel, or more spice if you want it bolder. No fitting category on the site, so I put it under Sides.

title: Air Fryer Chicken Chimichangas
ingredients: Avocado oil (for frying, brushing, or spraying)
steps: Mix the chicken, cream cheese, green chiles, salsa, cumin, garlic powder, garlic salt, and cheddar until well combined, with no cream cheese clumps.
Spoon the filling into the center of each tortilla, fold in the ends, and roll up like a burrito. Place seam side down.

Air fryer: Preheat to 390°F for 3 min. Brush or spray all sides with oil and place seam side down. Cook 4 min, flip, and cook 4-5 min more until browned. If a seam opens, secure with a toothpick or cook 1 more min seam side down.
Oven: Place seam side down on a greased baking sheet. Brush or spray well with oil. Bake at 400°F for 20-25 min until golden brown.
Skillet: Heat enough oil to cover the bottom of a skillet over medium heat. Cook seam side down 2-3 min until golden, then turn and cook all sides until crisp.
notes: Makes 6, about 15 minutes. The filling can be made up to 3 days ahead. Wrap and cook right before serving so the tortillas stay crisp. Serve on lettuce with salsa, sour cream, and cheese sauce.

title: Air Fryer Garlic Butter Steak Bites and Potatoes
ingredients: Olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and dried parsley, for the potatoes (no amounts given)
Salt, pepper and garlic powder (no amounts given)
Steak seasoning (Kinder's Prime Steak Seasoning), amount not given
steps: Wash the potatoes and cut into small cubes.
Toss the potatoes in olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder, paprika and dried parsley.
Air fry the potatoes at 400°F for about 20 minutes, shaking a couple of times. Set aside when done.
Cut the steak into 1 inch cubes and coat with olive oil, salt, pepper, garlic powder and steak seasoning.
Air fry the steak bites at 400°F for about 7 minutes (about medium).
Melt the butter and stir in the minced garlic and dried parsley.
Pour the garlic butter over the steak bites and serve over the potatoes.
notes: About 37 minutes total. Preheat the air fryer if it has that feature for a better sear. Pull the steak at 145°F; some reviewers found 7 minutes dry and did 4 to 6. Two 8 to 10 ounce steaks feed a family of four with the potatoes. Source gives no amounts for the seasonings.

title: Air Fryer Pork Belly Bites
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds pork belly (skin on or off), cut into 2 inch cubes
Teriyaki or sweet chili sauce, for dipping (optional)
steps: Mix the brown sugar, paprika, garlic powder, salt, pepper and olive oil in a large bowl.
Add the pork belly and toss until every piece is coated.
Preheat the air fryer to 400°F for 4 to 5 minutes, then add the pork in a single layer.
Air fry at 400°F for 15 minutes, turning halfway, until golden brown with some charred edges.
Serve warm, on their own or with dipping sauce.
notes: Serves 4 to 6. The pieces shrink a lot, so cut them big. Best eaten right away; leftovers keep 3 days and reheat in the air fryer at 350°F for 5 minutes. The source doesn't give an amount for the pepper.

title: Air Fryer White Fish with Garlic and Lemon Pepper
ingredients: 12 ounces tilapia fillets or other white fish (2 fillets, 6 ounces each)
Kosher or sea salt, to taste
Fresh cracked black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the air fryer to 360°F for 5 minutes. Rinse the fillets and pat dry.
Spray or coat the fish with olive oil spray and season both sides with the garlic powder, lemon pepper, onion powder, salt and pepper.
Lay perforated parchment in the basket (or spray the basket well) and lightly spray it so the fish doesn't stick.
Put the fish on the paper with a few lemon wedges alongside.
Air fry at 360°F for about 6 to 12 minutes, until the fish flakes with a fork. Time depends on thickness.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve warm with the toasted lemon wedges.
notes: Serves 2, about 15 minutes. Thicker fish like cod or halibut needs 1 to 2 more minutes. If the air fryer is already hot or you're cooking multiple batches, cut the time by a few minutes. Reviewers had good results with cod at 11 minutes and rockfish at 12.

title: Apple Cider Pork Chops
steps: Pat the pork chops dry with a paper towel and sprinkle both sides with salt and pepper. Heat the oil in a 10 inch skillet over medium-high heat until shimmering. Cook the chops about 4 minutes per side, until golden brown. Remove from the skillet.
In the same skillet, add the apple cider and brown sugar and cook until reduced by about half to a thick, syrupy glaze. Stir in the mustard and season with salt and pepper.
Pour the glaze over the pork chops to serve.
notes: Serves 4, about 25 minutes. Scrape up the brown bits when making the sauce for the most flavor. Good with rice and green beans. The source doesn't say how long to cook the chops through (4 minutes per side is for browning); check for 145°F.

title: Authentic Mexican Rice
ingredients: 2 teaspoons granulated tomato bouillon (or cubes; chicken bouillon works)
steps: Rinse the rice in a fine mesh strainer until the water runs clear.
Heat the oil in a large saucepan over medium-high heat. Add the rice and cook over medium heat, stirring often, until lightly golden all over, about 10 minutes.
Add the tomato sauce, garlic and onion and stir. Add the tomato bouillon, salt, carrot, peas, water and the serranos if using.
Bring to a boil, cover, reduce to low, and cook about 20 minutes until the water is absorbed.
Remove from the heat and rest 5 minutes, then fluff gently with a fork.
notes: Serves 6, about 35 minutes. Serranos go in whole for flavor, not heat; take them out before serving. Don't stir while cooking and do rest the rice before fluffing. For brown rice add 1/2 cup more water and cook 40 minutes. Can be made a day ahead; reheat covered with a splash of water.

title: Baked Chicken Parmesan
ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts (about 8 ounces each), sliced in half lengthwise to make 8 cutlets
steps: Preheat the oven to 450°F. Spray a large baking sheet.
Mix the breadcrumbs and parmesan in a bowl. Melt the butter in another bowl. Brush the butter lightly onto each cutlet, dip into the breadcrumbs, press to coat, and set on the baking sheet.
Spray the tops lightly with oil and bake 25 minutes, until golden.
Spoon about 1 tablespoon marinara over each cutlet and top with about 1 1/2 tablespoons mozzarella.
Bake 5 more minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbling. Garnish with basil or parsley.
notes: Serves 8 (1 cutlet each), about 40 minutes. Brushing with butter instead of an egg wash keeps it lighter. Good over pasta, zucchini noodles or with a salad, or on a roll as a sandwich. Freezer friendly.

title: Baked Rigatoni with Beef
ingredients: 1 (28 ounce) can crushed tomatoes with basil
1 pound part-skim mozzarella, cut into 1 inch cubes
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and spray a 9x13 baking dish. Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Warm 1/2 tablespoon oil in a saute pan over medium-high heat. Add the beef, season lightly, and brown 5 to 7 minutes, breaking it up. Move the beef to a plate and drain the pan.
Reduce to medium, add the remaining 2 tablespoons oil and the onion, and cook about 8 minutes until very soft. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute. Stir in the tomato paste.
Add the crushed tomatoes, broth, salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, about 15 minutes. Stir in the basil, cook 5 more minutes, then stir in the beef.
Meanwhile cook the rigatoni 8 to 9 minutes until just al dente. Drain and return to the pot, add the meat sauce, and stir well.
Pour into the baking dish and top with the cubed mozzarella.
Bake 30 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly. Garnish with fresh basil and serve warm.
notes: Serves 8, about 1 hour. Use all the sauce so the noodles stay tender. Italian sausage can replace the beef. Freezes up to 2 months; thaw 12 hours, then bake covered at 350°F for 30 minutes and uncovered 10 to 15 more. Serve with extra sauce, since freezing dries it out a bit.

title: Bourbon Chicken
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken (thighs or breasts)
2 tablespoons cornstarch (only if stir frying the chicken)
1/4 cup (2 ounces) apple sauce (or apple, pineapple or orange juice)
1/4 cup brown sugar (or honey or maple syrup)
1 teaspoon minced or grated fresh ginger
Garnish: 2 green onions, chopped, and 2 teaspoons toasted sesame seeds (optional)
steps: Heat the grill or oven if using one.
Whisk all the sauce ingredients together in a bowl.

Cook the chicken one of these ways, then keep it warm. Grill: toss with oil, salt and pepper, grill on medium high 3 to 4 minutes per side, rest 5 minutes, cut into bite-size pieces. Bake: oil, salt and pepper, bake at 425°F about 18 minutes, rest 5 minutes, cut up. Stir fry: cut into bite-size pieces, shake in a bag with 2 tablespoons cornstarch and 1/2 teaspoon salt, saute in oil on medium high in two batches, 4 to 5 minutes.
Heat a skillet on medium high, add the sauce, and cook, stirring, until it boils and thickens, 3 to 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and stir to coat. Lower the heat and cook 2 more minutes until heated through. Thin with a tablespoon or two of water or juice if too thick.
Serve over rice and garnish with green onions and sesame seeds.
notes: Serves 4. About 20 minutes. Sauce can be made ahead. Leftovers keep 2 to 3 days. A shortcut is to heat the sauce and stir in chopped rotisserie chicken. One reviewer said it tastes more like BBQ sauce than the mall version.

title: Boursin Cheese Pasta
ingredients: 1 5.3-ounce package garlic & fine herbs Boursin cheese
1/2 teaspoon kosher salt (plus more to taste)
8 ounces bow tie pasta (farfalle), or fusilli or rotini
Grated parmesan and more basil, for garnish (optional)
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. In a 9x13 ceramic casserole dish, put the Boursin in the middle and surround it with the tomatoes, red onion and garlic.
Drizzle with the olive oil, sprinkle with oregano, salt and pepper, and gently toss the vegetables to coat.
Bake 25 to 30 minutes, until the tomatoes burst and the onion softens.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta. Reserve 1/2 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

Stir the cheese and tomatoes together in the dish, gently squishing the tomatoes. Stir in the basil, then add the pasta and toss to coat. Add pasta water a little at a time to thin the sauce (1/4 cup was enough).
Serve right away with more basil and parmesan.
notes: Serves 4, about 40 minutes. To add chicken: season two 8 ounce chicken breasts with salt and pepper, set them on either side of the Boursin in the dish, bake about 35 minutes until 165°F. Leftovers keep up to 4 days. Good with spinach, sausage or shrimp added.

title: Brown Sugar Glazed Carrots
steps: Combine the carrots, water, butter and brown sugar in a pan over medium-high heat and bring to a boil.
Cover, reduce to low, and cook about 6 minutes.
Keeping it covered, turn the heat to high and cook, stirring now and then, until the liquid reduces to a glossy glaze and the carrots are fork-tender, another 5 to 8 minutes. Don't overcook.
Remove from the heat and season with salt and pepper.
notes: Serves 4, about 20 minutes. Whole carrots, peeled and cut into even sticks, cook more evenly than baby carrots according to one reviewer. Oven: 350°F covered for 1 hour. Slow cooker: HIGH 2 to 3 hours. Leftovers keep 2 to 3 days.

title: Cashew Chicken with Rice
ingredients: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1 inch cubes
Garnish: 1/2 cup chopped cashews, 2 green onions sliced, sriracha (optional)
steps: Cook the rice according to the package directions.
Stir together all the sauce ingredients and set aside.
Mix the cornstarch and salt in a medium bowl. Pat the chicken dry, cube it, and toss in the cornstarch mixture.
Heat a large skillet or wok over medium-high heat and add the vegetable and sesame oils. Cook the chicken 4 minutes until lightly browned, then remove.
Lower the heat to medium and cook the broccoli, carrots and red pepper about 5 minutes until barely tender. Return the chicken to the pan.
Pour in the sauce and cook a few more minutes. Add salt if needed.
Serve over the rice, topped with cashews, green onions and sriracha.
notes: Frozen veggies work in a pinch. Skip the nuts to make it nut-free. For gluten-free, use tamari or coconut aminos (go lightly with aminos).

title: Cheeseburger Soup
ingredients: Onion rings and thinly sliced green onions, for serving (optional)
steps: In a large saucepan over medium heat, cook and crumble the beef until no longer pink, 6 to 8 minutes. Drain and set the beef aside.
In the same pan, melt 1 tablespoon butter. Saute the onion, carrots, celery, basil and parsley about 10 minutes, until tender.
Add the potatoes, broth and beef. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer covered 10 to 12 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Meanwhile, melt the remaining 3 tablespoons butter in a small skillet. Add the flour and cook, stirring, 3 to 5 minutes until bubbly.
Stir the flour mixture into the soup, bring to a boil, and cook and stir 2 minutes.
Reduce the heat to low. Stir in the Velveeta, milk, salt and pepper and cook until the cheese melts.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the sour cream. Serve with onion rings and green onions if you like.
notes: Makes 8 servings (about 2 quarts). Prep 30 min, cook 25 min. FLAG: the saved link (cheeseburger-paradise-soup) now redirects to Taste of Home's recipe titled "Cheeseburger Soup", so this is that recipe, not necessarily the "Paradise" one you saved. Use lean beef or drain well. Remove the pot from the heat before adding sour cream so it does not curdle. Do not freeze (the dairy turns grainy). Fridge leftovers keep up to 4 days. Velveeta amount is a range, 8 oz for less cheesy and 16 oz for very cheesy. Common add-ons: crumbled bacon, pickles, tomatoes.

title: Cheesy Hasselback Potatoes (Mario Batali)
ingredients: 4 tbsp butter (1 tbsp for the baking dish, the rest dotted on top)
1 lb Gruyere, cut into 1/4-inch-thick slices, then into 2-inch squares
1/4 cup thinly sliced prosciutto, cut into ribbons
Salt and freshly ground black pepper
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter a baking dish with 1 tbsp of the butter.
Microwave the potatoes on high for 8 to 10 minutes. Set aside until cool enough to handle.

Lay a potato on a cutting board and use a serrated knife to cut slits about 1/4 inch apart, leaving about 1/2 inch uncut at the bottom. Resting two wooden spoons on either side of the potato keeps the knife from cutting through. Repeat with the other potatoes.
Set the potatoes in the baking dish. Tuck a square of Gruyere into each slit and season with salt and pepper.
Whisk the milk, sour cream and nutmeg together and pour over the potatoes.
Mix the prosciutto, Parmigiano-Reggiano and panko and sprinkle over the top. Dot with the remaining butter.
Bake 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and crispy on top and the potatoes are cooked through. Top with chives.
notes: Serves 4. FLAG: the saved ABC The Chew link no longer opens. This is a newspaper reprint of Mario Batali's recipe from the show. The reprint skips the line where the milk, sour cream and nutmeg are mixed before being poured over the potatoes, so step 5 is an assumption. It also does not say when the chives go in; sprinkling them on at the end is an assumption. Source says to butter the dish with 1 tbsp of the butter and 'scatter' butter on top without giving the split; the rest (3 tbsp) is assumed. Not the same as the earlier 'Fully Loaded Hasselback Potatoes' entry.

title: Cheesy Scalloped Potatoes and Ham
ingredients: 2 cups nonfat milk (plus up to 1/4 cup more if the sauce is too thick)
2 1/4 cups freshly shredded cheddar cheese, divided
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a 13x9 baking pan with cooking spray.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil. Scrub the potatoes and boil them whole for about 20 minutes. Remove and let cool until easy to handle.
Melt the butter in a medium saucepan over medium heat. Whisk in the flour and cook, whisking constantly, until golden, about 2 minutes.
Stir in the milk and cook, stirring often, until thickened, 2 to 3 minutes. Remove from the heat, stir in 2 cups of the cheddar, and season with salt and pepper.
Peel the potatoes and slice into 1/8 inch rounds.
Layer 1/3 of the potatoes in the dish, overlapping, and season with salt and pepper. Top with half the ham and about 1/3 of the cheese sauce.
Repeat with a second layer of potatoes, ham and sauce. Finish with the last of the potatoes and pour the remaining sauce over the top, spreading to cover.
Sprinkle with the remaining 1/4 cup cheddar and 1/8 to 1/4 teaspoon paprika.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbly. Garnish with chives and serve right away.
notes: Serves 6 as a main, 8 to 10 as a side. Boiling the potatoes first is what keeps them evenly creamy. Can be baked ahead, cooled, wrapped, and refrigerated 2 to 3 days; reheat at 350°F for 25 to 35 minutes. Freezes up to 4 months. Source gives no amounts for salt and pepper.

title: Chicken Fried Rice (Robert Irvine)
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Vegetable oil, for frying (very little for the omelettes, 3 tbsp for the chicken and onion, 2 tbsp more for the rice)
4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves, cut into thin strips
6 green onions, thinly sliced, plus more for garnish (optional)
steps: Whisk the eggs in a small bowl and season with salt and pepper. Heat a very little oil in a medium pan over medium heat and make a thin omelette with half the eggs. Turn it out onto a plate without folding. Repeat with the rest of the eggs.
Stack one omelette on the other, fold, and chop coarsely. Set aside.
Toss the chicken strips with the sesame oil and season with salt and pepper.
Heat 3 tbsp vegetable oil in a large pan or wok over high heat. Stir-fry the chicken until lightly golden, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the onion and garlic and stir-fry 1 to 2 minutes, until the onion softens.
Add 2 tbsp more oil, and when hot, stir in the cold rice and green onions. Toss until very hot.
Sprinkle with the soy sauce and mix evenly. Take off the heat, stir in the chopped egg, and garnish with more green onions if you like.
notes: Yield 6 to 8 servings. Prep 10 min, cook 15 min. Use cold, day-old rice. Source gives no amounts for the salt and pepper and does not name a type of rice.

title: Chicken Lo Mein
ingredients: 1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into small pieces
16 ounces lo mein noodles (or other Asian-style noodles)
steps: Cook the noodles per the package, drain, and set aside.
Whisk all the sauce ingredients in a small bowl.
Toss the chicken with the soy sauce, ginger and garlic.
Heat 2 tablespoons olive oil in a large, very hot wok. Cook the chicken about 5 minutes until browned and no longer pink, in 2 batches if needed so it does not crowd. Move to a plate.
Add the other 2 tablespoons oil, then the mushrooms, cabbage, carrots and onion. Cook about 1 minute, tossing.
Return the chicken, add the noodles and the sauce, and toss to coat. Turn off the heat.
Garnish with green onions and serve.
notes: Serves 6. Prep 15 min, cook 15 min. Dark soy sauce gives the color and richer flavor (regular soy works but is lighter). Spaghetti, ramen or linguine work if you have no lo mein noodles. Double the sauce if you want it saucy or plan on leftovers. Fridge leftovers keep 3 to 4 days, add a splash of water or broth when reheating. Freezing is not recommended (noodles go mushy). The saved link redirects to jocooks.com/recipes/chicken-lo-mein/.

title: Chicken Lo Mein with Angel Hair and Hoisin
ingredients: 1 medium onion, halved lengthwise and thinly sliced
1 cup sugar snap pea pods, halved
1 (15 oz) can Chinese baby corn, drained and cut in thirds (optional)
1 to 1 1/4 lb skinless, boneless chicken breast, cut into bite-size strips
steps: Cook the noodles until just tender. Drain, rinse with cold water, drain well, and set aside.
In a small bowl, mix the hoisin sauce, chicken broth, soy sauce, sesame oil and cornstarch. Set aside.
Heat 1 tbsp of the vegetable oil in a large pan or wok. Stir-fry the ginger for 30 seconds, then add the onion and stir-fry 2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and carrots and stir-fry 2 more minutes. Add the broccoli, pea pods and baby corn and stir-fry 2 more minutes. Move the vegetables to a plate.

Heat the remaining 1 tbsp oil in the pan. Stir-fry half the chicken until no longer pink, 3 to 4 minutes, then move it to a plate. Stir-fry the rest of the chicken, then return the first batch to the pan.
Add the noodles, vegetables and sauce and turn the heat down to medium. Gently toss with two spatulas until heated through, about 3 minutes.
notes: Serves 6 to 8. FLAG: the saved link was a POPSUGAR/YumSugar page (Fast Easy Dinner: Chicken Lo Mein) that now redirects to an unrelated site. The ingredients are from a copy of that recipe on Just A Pinch; the steps are from a Cookpad copy of the same FamilyFun recipe (same ingredient list), so the wording is not the original's. The earlier 'Chicken Lo Mein' entry is a different recipe.

title: Creamy Chicken Pesto Pasta
ingredients: 1 pound asparagus, ends trimmed and cut into 2 inch pieces
steps: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water according to the package. Don't rinse it.

Cut the chicken breasts in half lengthwise and season with 1/2 teaspoon salt and the pepper. Heat 2 tablespoons oil in a large deep skillet over medium heat and cook the chicken 3 minutes per side until cooked through. Rest 5 minutes, then slice into strips.
Add 2 tablespoons oil and the asparagus to the same pan and saute 2 to 3 minutes until crisp tender.
Add the cream, bring to a simmer, and cook 3 minutes. Stir in the pesto, add the chicken, and cook 2 minutes. Don't boil or the sauce can separate. Season with the remaining 1/2 teaspoon salt.
Add the cooked pasta, stir to coat, and serve right away. Garnish with basil or parsley.
notes: Serves 8 as written (about 30 minutes). Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days; reheat on low with a splash of cream or broth. Store-bought pesto works fine. Rotisserie chicken can replace the chicken breasts (skip the chicken-cooking step).

title: Creamy Chicken Wild Rice Soup
ingredients: 2 cups thinly sliced celery (3 to 4 stalks)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large stockpot over medium heat. Add the onion, carrot, celery, mushrooms, garlic, thyme, rosemary, oregano, salt and pepper. Cook, stirring occasionally, 10 minutes.
Sprinkle the flour over the vegetables and stir to coat. Cook, stirring constantly, 2 minutes, scraping up anything stuck to the pan.
Stir in the chicken stock, water, wild rice and chicken. Bring to a simmer, reduce to low, cover, and cook 45 minutes, stirring occasionally. Check that the rice is done.
Stir in the cream, taste, and add more salt and pepper as needed. Keep warm until serving.
notes: Makes 8 servings, about 1 hour 15 minutes. Cook time doesn't include cooking the chicken. Leftovers keep 3 days in the fridge.

title: Creamy Garlic Mushrooms and Bacon
ingredients: 26 ounces brown mushrooms, washed and patted dry
1/4 cup dry white wine or chicken broth
Salt and pepper, a pinch of each
steps: Fry the bacon in a large oven-safe skillet over medium heat until crispy. Move to a paper towel lined plate with a slotted spoon.
In the same pan, melt the butter. Add the mushrooms, drizzle with the oil, scrape up the browned bits, and fry 2 to 3 minutes until lightly browned.
Pour in the wine or broth and let it reduce 2 minutes, stirring now and then. Preheat the broiler.

Add the garlic and stir about 1 minute until fragrant. Pour in the cream, parsley and thyme, lower the heat, and simmer gently 4 to 5 minutes until the mushrooms are tender and the sauce thickens. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir the bacon back in and top with the mozzarella and parmesan.
Broil 3 to 5 minutes until the cheese is melted and bubbly. Serve warm.
notes: Serves 8 as a side, about 40 minutes. Use a wide pan so the mushrooms brown. Season at the end since the bacon and parmesan are salty. Works over steak, chicken or pasta.

title: Creamy Mushroom Wild Rice
ingredients: 1 cup wild rice (quick-cook wild rice blend, see notes)
steps: Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the onion and mushrooms and cook, stirring occasionally, until soft.
Add the garlic and stir 1 minute. Season with salt, pepper and Italian seasoning.
Add the broth and rice, bring to a boil, then reduce to low, cover, and simmer 15 minutes.
Remove from the heat and let stand covered 5 minutes.
Uncover and stir in the cream and parmesan until the cheese melts.
notes: Serves 6, about 25 minutes. The 15 minute time is for a quick-cook wild rice blend. Regular wild rice can take about 45 minutes, so check the package. Long grain white rice, basmati or jasmine also work.

title: Crispy Sheet Pan Gnocchi and Veggies
ingredients: 1 (12 ounce) bag mixed baby bell peppers (or 2 medium bell peppers)
1 pound fresh, shelf-stable, or frozen potato gnocchi
2 tablespoons olive oil, plus more for drizzling
Grated Pecorino Romano or parmesan, for serving
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F with a rack in the middle. Line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.
In a large bowl, combine the bell peppers cut into 1 inch chunks, the red onion halved and thinly sliced, the garlic minced, and 1 teaspoon coarsely chopped rosemary leaves.
Add the gnocchi (straight from the package, no boiling), tomatoes, salt and a few grinds of pepper. Drizzle with 2 tablespoons olive oil and toss gently. Spread in an even layer on the baking sheet.
Roast, stirring halfway, until the gnocchi are plump and the vegetables are tender and browning, 18 to 20 minutes.
Right out of the oven, tear the burrata and basil over the top. Sprinkle with Pecorino or parmesan and red pepper flakes, and drizzle with more olive oil if you like.
notes: Serves 4, about 25 minutes. The ingredient list says 1/4 teaspoon salt but the step says 1/2, so I used 1/2. Roasted gnocchi gets crispy outside and chewy inside rather than light. Leftovers keep up to 4 days.

title: Crock Pot Cashew Chicken (Daydream Kitchen)
ingredients: 2 pounds boneless, skinless chicken thigh tenders or chicken breast tenders
steps: Combine the flour and pepper in a large zip bag, add the chicken, and shake to coat.
Heat the oil in a skillet over medium-high heat and brown the chicken about 2 minutes on each side.
Put the chicken in the slow cooker.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, ketchup, brown sugar, garlic, ginger and red pepper flakes in a small bowl and pour over the chicken.
Cook on LOW 3 to 4 hours.
Stir in the cashews and serve over rice.
notes: FLAG: the Daydream Kitchen page itself was not opened; the amounts and steps come from two copies (a blog post and a Just A Pinch copy that links back to it), which match. One copy says it serves 4. If you want sauce to pour over the rice, double the sauce ingredients (a tip on the Just A Pinch copy).

title: Crockpot Chicken and Rice
ingredients: 1 cup long-grain brown rice (no other kind of rice)
1 1/2 pounds boneless skinless chicken breasts or thighs
1/2 cup freshly grated sharp cheddar, divided
steps: Rinse the rice several times. Boil 2 cups of the broth, add the rice, cook 10 minutes, then drain.

Coat a 5-quart or larger slow cooker with nonstick spray. Add the rice, carrots, shallot and Dijon and stir. Lay the chicken on top and sprinkle with the garlic powder, thyme, salt and pepper. Pour in 2 1/2 cups broth.
Cover and cook on HIGH 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the chicken is cooked through.

Remove the chicken to a plate and cover. Stir the rice mixture, re-cover, and cook on high until the rice is tender, about 1 to 1 1/2 more hours. Splash in some of the remaining broth if it looks dry.
Stir in the peas and Greek yogurt. Dice the chicken and stir it in with 1/4 cup of the cheddar. Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top, cover a few minutes until melted, and serve with parsley.
notes: Serves 4. Must cook on HIGH (low gives mushy rice). Thaw the chicken first. Pull the chicken at 160°F. Slow cookers vary a lot, so plan on extra time the first go; rice can take longer. Leftovers keep 4 days, freeze up to 3 months. Reviews are mixed on how the rice turns out.

title: Denver Omelet Egg Muffins
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F and grease a muffin tin (silicone releases easiest).
In a medium bowl, beat the eggs, cream, baking powder, salt and pepper until fully combined.
Stir in the ham, cheese, onion and bell pepper until evenly distributed.
Scoop 1/4 cup of the mixture into each muffin cup.
Bake 18 to 20 minutes, until set and a toothpick comes out clean.
notes: Makes 12, about 25 minutes. Fridge up to 5 days; reheat in the microwave in 15 second bursts. Freezes well: cool completely, freeze on a plate, then bag; reheat in 30 second bursts. Source says the salt amount covers the pepper too, so the pepper amount is unspecified. Pepper jack instead of cheddar adds spice.

title: Easy Shrimp and Broccoli Stir Fry
ingredients: 1 1/2 pounds medium shrimp, peeled and deveined
steps: Whisk the soy sauce, oyster sauce, rice wine vinegar, brown sugar, ginger, garlic, sesame oil, cornstarch and Sriracha (if using) in a small bowl.
Heat the olive oil in a large cast iron skillet over medium-high. Cook the shrimp, stirring occasionally, until pink, 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the broccoli and cook, stirring often, until tender, 2 to 3 minutes.
Stir in the sauce until combined and slightly thickened, 1 to 2 minutes.
Serve right away, garnished with green onion and sesame seeds.
notes: Serves 4. Prep 10 min, cook 10 min. Serve with brown rice (the rice takes longer than the dish). Many readers double the sauce. If you want the broccoli more cooked, start it first and add the shrimp after so they do not overcook.

title: Fully Loaded Hasselback Potatoes
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F (200°C).
Slice the potatoes thinly (about 1/8 inch) without cutting all the way through. Setting a wooden spoon or similar at the base of the potato helps stop the knife.
Put the potatoes on a baking sheet, tuck the sliced butter and garlic between a few of the cuts, and season with salt and pepper.
Roast until crispy on top and tender in the middle, about 1 hour.
Meanwhile cook the bacon until crispy and crumble it.
Sprinkle the potatoes with the cheese and bacon and return to the oven about 5 minutes, until the cheese melts. Watch them so the cheese does not melt off into the pan.
Serve topped with sour cream and green onions.
notes: Serves 4 (a side with small potatoes, a meal with larger ones). Prep 10 min, cook 1 hr 5 min, total 1 hr 15 min. The 551 calorie figure on the page is per potato. Reader tips: slice between two chopsticks or thin cutting boards so you cannot cut through, and rinse the sliced potato to remove starch so the slices do not stick.

title: Garlic Butter Chicken Bites with Lemon Asparagus
ingredients: 3 boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into bite-sized chunks
1/2 cup butter, divided (1/4 cup for the chicken, 1/4 cup for the sauce)
1 teaspoon Italian seasoning or Herbes de Provence
Chicken seasoning: 1 teaspoon salt, 1 teaspoon black pepper, 2 teaspoons onion powder
steps: Season the chicken chunks with the salt, pepper and onion powder and let sit on a plate.
Blanch the trimmed asparagus in boiling water 2 minutes, then move to ice water. Drain. Skip this if the asparagus is skinny.

Melt 1/4 cup butter with the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat. Brown the chicken on all sides in batches, so it doesn't steam. Lower the heat, add 1 teaspoon garlic and the Italian seasoning, and cook 1 minute. Move the chicken to a plate.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the remaining teaspoon of garlic, and deglaze with the chicken broth. Simmer until reduced by half.
Stir in the remaining 1/4 cup butter, lemon juice, hot sauce and parsley.
Add the asparagus and toss 2 minutes. Push it aside, return the chicken, and stir 1 minute to reheat.
Garnish with more parsley, pepper flakes and lemon slices and serve right away.
notes: Serves 4, about 30 minutes. Good over rice or cauliflower rice. Broccoli, green beans or zucchini can replace the asparagus. A splash of white wine can replace some of the broth. Chicken bites are done in 5 to 6 minutes (165°F).

title: Garlic Chicken and Potatoes (Food Network Kitchen)
ingredients: 3 tbsp extra-virgin olive oil (1 tbsp for the potatoes, 2 tbsp for the garlic mixture)
3/4 tsp kosher salt, for the potatoes, plus more for the chicken
4 skinless, boneless chicken breasts (1 1/2 to 1 3/4 lb)
2 tbsp chopped fresh cilantro or parsley
steps: Put a rack in the lower third of the oven and heat to 425°F.
Toss the potatoes with 1 tbsp olive oil, the cumin seeds, 3/4 tsp salt and pepper. Spread in a large baking dish and roast 25 to 30 minutes, until they start to brown.
Meanwhile, heat the remaining 2 tbsp olive oil in a small skillet over medium heat. Cook the garlic, stirring often, until lightly golden, about 2 minutes.
Take the skillet off the heat and stir in the brown sugar, lemon juice and red pepper flakes.
Take the baking dish out of the oven, push the potatoes to the sides and put the chicken in the middle. Season the chicken with salt and drizzle with the garlic mixture.
Return to the oven and bake about 20 minutes, until the chicken is cooked through and the potatoes are tender.
Move the chicken to a cutting board and slice. Toss the cilantro with the potatoes in the baking dish. Serve the chicken with the potatoes and lemon wedges, and drizzle with the pan juices.
notes: Serves 4. Total 40 min, active 20 min. Source gives no amounts for the pepper or the salt on the chicken.

title: Garlic Mushroom Chicken Bites
ingredients: 1 pound boneless chicken thighs, cut into 1 inch pieces
1 tablespoon seeded, chopped green bell pepper
steps: Heat 1 tablespoon oil in a large pan over medium-high heat. Add the chicken, season with salt, pepper, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, onion powder and paprika, and sear until browned and cooked through, 5 to 6 minutes. Move to a plate and keep warm.
Heat the remaining oil and 1 tablespoon butter in the same pan. Add the mushrooms and cook, stirring, 3 to 4 minutes until just starting to brown and soften.
Add the remaining butter. When melted, saute the shallot and bell pepper about 3 minutes until soft, then add the garlic for about 30 seconds.
Return the chicken with its juices and toss to coat. Cook 1 to 2 more minutes until the vegetables are soft and the chicken is cooked through.
Taste, adjust the salt and pepper, and serve warm with the parsley.
notes: Serves 4 to 6, about 30 minutes. Chicken is done at 165°F. Add chili powder, red pepper flakes or sriracha for heat. Good on toothpicks as an appetizer.

title: Garlic Parmesan Chicken Thighs
ingredients: 3 cloves garlic, minced (or 2 teaspoons garlic powder)
Salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F and spray a 9x13 baking dish with nonstick spray.
In one shallow dish, mix the olive oil and garlic. In a second, mix the bread crumbs, parmesan, Italian seasoning and oregano.
Season the chicken with salt and pepper. Dip each thigh in the oil, then dredge in the crumb mixture, and place in the baking dish.
Bake 30 minutes, until a thermometer in the thickest part reads 165°F.
Broil 2 minutes to brown the cheese. Garnish with parsley.
notes: About 45 minutes. If you use garlic powder instead of fresh, mix it into the crumbs, not the oil. Some reviewers found the thighs needed up to 45 minutes to reach temperature, and some had leftover crumb mixture. Works with bone-in thighs (longer time) and in the air fryer (about 15 minutes).

title: Garlic Parmesan Roasted Carrots
ingredients: 4 large cloves garlic, minced (or 1 tablespoon minced garlic)
Salt and pepper, a pinch of each to taste
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F and lightly grease a baking sheet.
Spread the carrots on the sheet in a single layer with a little space between them. Add the olive oil, garlic, parmesan, breadcrumbs, salt and pepper and toss to coat.
Bake 20 to 25 minutes, tossing halfway, until fork tender and golden.
Serve right away, topped with parsley.
notes: Serves 6, about 30 minutes. Dry the carrots well and cut them evenly so they crisp. Air fryer: 390°F for 12 to 15 minutes, shaking halfway. Best fresh; leftovers keep 3 to 4 days and reheat at 400°F.

title: Glazed Chicken and Broccoli Sheet Pan Dinner
ingredients: 3/4 pound (about 3 cups) fingerling potatoes, halved lengthwise
Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
1 medium head broccoli, cut into small florets (about 4 cups)
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and line a rimmed baking sheet with parchment.

Put the drumsticks on one side of the sheet, spaced apart. Put the potatoes on the other side, leaving the center open for the broccoli. Drizzle the potatoes with 1 tablespoon of the oil and sprinkle with salt and pepper, tossing to coat.
Roast the drumsticks and potatoes for about 20 minutes (see notes).

Take the sheet out and put the broccoli in the center. Drizzle with the remaining 2 tablespoons oil, season lightly with salt and pepper, and toss with tongs. Brush the drumsticks all over with the teriyaki glaze.
Return to the oven and roast 20 to 25 minutes more, until the broccoli and potatoes are tender and charred in spots and the drumsticks are cooked through (the recipe says 160°F).
Divide the chicken and vegetables between two plates.
notes: Serves 2. Total 55 min, 15 min active. FLAG: the first roast time was missing from the text I could get (the fetched version jumps from step 1 to "20 to 25 minutes more"). 20 minutes is from a blog that adapted this recipe, and it fits the 55 minute total, but confirm against the original if you can. The source says drumsticks are done at 160°F, USDA's guidance for poultry is 165°F, so you may want to go to 165°F. Salt and pepper amounts are not given. A blog adaptation doubled it onto two sheets with Yukon Gold potatoes and tossed the cooked broccoli in a little extra teriyaki. The saved link is a short form of the Food Network URL; the live page has -3543898 appended.

title: Glazed Ham and Cheese Sliders (Hawaiian Rolls)
ingredients: 1 package (12 count) King's Hawaiian Sweet Rolls
12 slices smoked ham (about 1/2 pound, thinly sliced or shaved)
12 slices Monterey Jack or Colby Jack cheese (about 1/4 pound)
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F.
Melt the butter with the brown sugar, Worcestershire and mustard in a small pot, stirring until smooth.
Keeping the rolls attached, slice them in half horizontally. Brush the glaze generously onto both cut sides, saving a little for the tops.
Put the bottom halves in a 9x13 baking dish. Layer the ham, then the cheese. Add the tops and brush with the leftover glaze. Sprinkle with poppy seeds if using.
Cover tightly with foil and bake 25 minutes, until the cheese is melted.
Slice and serve, with warmed raspberry preserves on the side if you like.
notes: Makes 12, about 35 minutes. Can be assembled the night before; add a few minutes baking from cold. Cut the bottom half a bit thicker so it doesn't get soggy. A reviewer suggested adding the glaze right before baking if making ahead. Leftovers are good cold or microwaved. Works with turkey instead of ham.

title: Grilled Bruschetta Chicken
ingredients: 4 boneless skinless chicken breasts, pounded to an even thickness (1 inch or less)
steps: In a large bowl, toss the chicken with the oil, Italian seasoning, garlic powder, salt and pepper until evenly coated.
Grill over medium-high heat 6 to 8 minutes per side, until cooked through.
Meanwhile, stir the tomatoes, lemon juice, basil, salt and pepper together in a bowl.
Top each chicken breast with a slice of mozzarella and grill about 1 more minute until melted.
Top with the tomato basil mixture and serve right away.
notes: Serves 4, about 30 minutes. The tomato topping can be made ahead and kept in the fridge. The source's written steps skip the salt, but the ingredient list calls for 1/2 teaspoon, so I added it to step 1.

title: Homemade Hamburger Helper
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the oil in a large stockpot or Dutch oven over medium-high. Brown the beef 3 to 5 minutes, crumbling it, and season with salt and pepper. Drain the excess fat.
Add the mushrooms and cook 3 to 4 minutes until tender and browned. Stir in the tomato paste about 1 minute until lightly browned, then the flour about 1 minute.
Stir in the beef broth and egg noodles. Bring to a boil, cover, reduce the heat, and simmer 10 to 12 minutes until the noodles are cooked.
Stir in the sour cream and Dijon until combined.
Serve right away, garnished with parsley.
notes: Serves 4. Prep 10 min, cook 20 min, one pot. Plain Greek yogurt can replace the sour cream. Some readers found the Dijon strong and used less (about 1/2 teaspoon) or more sour cream. Peas are a popular add-in. Doubles easily.

title: Hot Chicken Philly Cheesesteak Dip
steps: Preheat the oven to 350°F. Season the chicken with salt and pepper on both sides.
Spray a grill pan or large skillet with cooking spray and cook the chicken over high heat about 1 minute per side, until cooked through. Slice thin and set aside.
Spray more oil in the pan and saute the onions and peppers over medium-low heat 5 to 6 minutes until soft.
Combine all the ingredients in a medium bowl.
Put in an oven-proof dish and bake 20 to 25 minutes, until hot and the cheese is melted.
notes: Makes 12 servings of 1/4 cup, about 45 minutes. Can be assembled a day ahead and refrigerated before baking. Serve with toasted baguette slices, bagel thins, pretzel thins, tortilla chips or veggies. The author tried Greek yogurt in place of sour cream but preferred the light sour cream.

title: Lighter Broccoli Beef
ingredients: 1 1/4 pounds flank or sirloin steak, sliced very thin against the grain
1/2 cup + 2 tablespoons reduced-sodium tamari or soy sauce, divided
2 1/2 tablespoons cornstarch (or gluten free flour), divided
1/2 teaspoon ground ginger (or 1 teaspoon ginger paste)
steps: In a zip bag, combine the sliced steak, 2 tablespoons tamari and 1 tablespoon cornstarch. Seal, squish to coat, and refrigerate while you prep.

Whisk together the remaining 1/2 cup tamari, remaining 1 1/2 tablespoons cornstarch, chicken broth, brown sugar, 2 tablespoons water, rice vinegar, sesame oil, garlic, ginger and chili flakes. Set aside.
Heat a large wok or nonstick skillet on high. Add 1/4 cup water, and when it simmers add the broccoli and stir fry 2 to 3 minutes until crisp tender. Move to a plate.

Heat 1 tablespoon oil until very hot. Add half the beef in a single layer, let it sit 30 seconds to brown, then stir fry until barely cooked through (a little pink is fine). Move to the plate. Repeat with the remaining oil and beef.
Pour the sauce into the wok and simmer 2 to 3 minutes until slightly thickened.
Return the beef and broccoli, simmer about 1 minute until heated through, and serve over rice.
notes: Serves 4, about 25 minutes. Have everything ready before you start; the cooking only takes 5 to 7 minutes. Gluten free if you use tamari and gluten free broth.

title: Lo Mian (Egg Noodles with Beef and Chinese Broccoli)
ingredients: 3 tbsp light soy sauce (1 tbsp for the marinade, 2 tbsp for the sauce)
3 tbsp oyster sauce (1 tbsp for the marinade, 2 tbsp for the sauce)
1/2 lb top sirloin steak, halved lengthwise and thinly sliced
1/2 lb Chinese broccoli, trimmed, leaves and stems thinly sliced on the diagonal
1 lb dan mian (fresh thick egg noodles)
steps: Stir 1 tbsp light soy sauce, 1 tbsp oyster sauce and the sugar together in a bowl. Add the beef and marinate for 20 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok over high heat. Stir-fry the beef until it starts to brown.
Add the Chinese broccoli and stir-fry until tender, about 3 minutes. Move the beef and broccoli to a plate.
In the same wok, bring the stock, the remaining 2 tbsp light soy sauce, the remaining 2 tbsp oyster sauce and the dark soy sauce to a boil over high heat.
Add the noodles, stir, and cook until most of the liquid is absorbed, 5 to 10 minutes.
Stir in the sesame oil, beef and broccoli. Season with pepper and serve.
notes: Serves 4. FLAG: the saved link was an old MSN address that could not be opened. This is the Saveur recipe with the same title, so it is very likely the same one, but it is not confirmed. Source gives no amount for the pepper. Fresh thick egg noodles are sold in the refrigerated section of Asian grocery stores; Chinese broccoli is also called gai lan.

title: Loaded Reese’s Peanut Butter Dip
ingredients: 2/3 cup mini peanut butter cups, chopped
Extra mini peanut butter cups, chopped (topping)
steps: Mix the softened cream cheese, peanut butter, brown sugar, vanilla, and salt in a large bowl with an electric mixer until fully combined.
Fold in the Cool Whip until combined.
Stir in the mini Reese’s Pieces and chopped peanut butter cups.
Transfer to a serving dish.
Top with more Reese’s Pieces and chopped peanut butter cups right before serving.
notes: Serves 10, about 15 minutes. Serve with graham crackers, pretzels, vanilla wafers, apple slices, or strawberries. Chill 20-30 min for a thicker dip. Keeps 4 days in the fridge. Do not leave out more than 2 hours. Do not freeze.

title: Maple Roasted Butternut Squash
ingredients: 8 cups peeled, seeded butternut squash cut into 1-inch cubes (about 3 pounds of peeled cubes)
steps: Heat the oven to 425°F. Line two rimmed baking sheets with parchment or foil (optional but it makes cleanup easier).

Spread the squash in a single layer across both sheets. On each sheet, drizzle 1 tablespoon oil and 1 tablespoon maple syrup, then sprinkle 1/4 teaspoon salt, 1/4 teaspoon cinnamon and a pinch of cayenne.
Toss to coat and roast about 30 minutes, swapping the sheets between racks halfway, until the largest piece is fork-tender.
Turn on the broiler. If you used parchment, slide the squash onto the bare sheet first (parchment should not go under the broiler).
Broil each sheet 1 to 2 minutes, watching closely, until golden brown. Serve warm.
notes: Serves 6. Prep 5 min, cook 35 min. Vegan, dairy free, gluten free. A large squash (or two smaller) of about 3 lb 3 oz whole weight gives about 8 cups of peeled cubes. It looks like a lot but it shrinks. Halves easily for two people. It browns fast under the broiler, so do not walk away. One reader found the top burned early at 425°F, so check at 15 minutes. The saved link redirects to toriavey.com/maple-cinnamon-roasted-butternut-squash/.

title: Meatball Stroganoff Pasta Casserole
ingredients: 1 bag (12 oz) uncooked extra-wide egg noodles (about 7 cups)
2 packages (8 oz each) white mushrooms, sliced
4 oz cream cheese, softened and cut into small cubes
1 package (22 oz) frozen cooked beef meatballs, thawed
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F. Spray a 13x9-inch (3-quart) baking dish with cooking spray.
Cook the noodles using the minimum time on the package, drain, and set aside.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a 12-inch skillet over medium-high. Cook the mushrooms and onion 3 to 5 minutes, stirring now and then, until the onion is tender.
Sprinkle the flour over the mushrooms and onion and stir well. Gradually stir in the beef broth, then add the Worcestershire, salt and pepper.
Bring to a simmer, stirring occasionally, and cook 3 to 5 minutes until slightly thickened.
Whisk in the cream cheese until mostly incorporated (small bits are fine, they melt in the oven). Remove from the heat and stir in the cream.
In the baking dish, combine the noodles, sauce and meatballs, mixing to coat.
Cover and bake 30 to 35 minutes, until bubbling and heated through. Stir, cool 10 minutes, stir again before serving, and garnish with parsley.
notes: Serves 10. Prep 30 min, total 1 hr 15 min. Stirring before serving spreads the sauce evenly. Good with a green vegetable or side salad. The original uses Progresso beef flavored broth, but any beef broth works.

title: Moroccan Chicken
ingredients: 1/4 cup Land O Lakes Cinnamon Sugar Butter Spread
1 small (1/2 cup) yellow onion, thinly sliced
1 medium (1 cup) red bell pepper, cut into strips
1 pound boneless skinless chicken breasts, cut into 1 inch pieces
Cooked rice or couscous, for serving (optional)
steps: Melt the cinnamon sugar butter spread in a 12 inch skillet until sizzling. Add the onion and cook over medium-high heat 2 to 3 minutes until crisp-tender. Add the bell pepper and cook 2 to 3 minutes more.
Add the chicken, garlic, salt and cayenne. Cook, stirring occasionally, 5 to 7 minutes until the chicken is browned and no longer pink.
Add the orange juice and raisins and cook, stirring, 1 to 2 minutes until heated through. Stir in the cilantro.
Serve right away over rice or couscous.
notes: Serves 4, about 25 minutes. Uses cinnamon sugar butter spread, a specific product; if you can't find it, use regular butter with a pinch of cinnamon and sugar (my substitution, not from the source).

title: Mushroom Asiago Chicken
ingredients: Salt and pepper, for the cutlets (no amount given)
1/2 cup dry white wine (or chicken broth)
3 teaspoons fresh thyme (sprigs), or dried thyme (see notes)
steps: Cut each chicken breast into cutlets. Lightly season both sides with salt and pepper and dredge in flour, shaking off the excess.

Melt about 2 tablespoons butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the cutlets in batches (do not crowd) about 5 minutes until golden on the first side, flip and cook 1 more minute. Move to a plate and cover loosely with foil.
Add the remaining butter, the mushrooms and 1/2 teaspoon salt to the skillet. Cook about 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until golden and softened. Add the garlic and cook 2 more minutes.

Pour in the wine (or 1/2 cup broth) and scrape up the browned bits. When it has nearly all evaporated, add the 3/4 cup broth and thyme. Boil, then reduce to medium and cook at a rapid simmer 10 to 15 minutes until reduced by half.

Reduce the heat to medium-low and stir in the cream. Sprinkle in the Asiago and stir constantly until it melts. Nestle the chicken back in and simmer just until heated through and the sauce slightly thickens.
Sprinkle with Parmesan and serve, plain or over pasta or mashed potatoes.
notes: Serves 5 to 6. Prep 15 min, cook 35 min (about 50 total). Be patient with the reduction step, the sauce should be down by half before the chicken goes back in. FLAG: the thyme line reads "3 tsp fresh thyme, sprigs, or 3/4 dried thyme leaves" with no unit on the dried amount, so I assumed 3/4 teaspoon dried, confirm if you can. Any mushroom works (button or cremini). Sherry, port or marsala can replace the wine. Readers double the sauce when serving over pasta, and add spinach, bacon or kale. Salt and pepper for the cutlets have no amount in the source.

title: Oatmeal Cinnamon French Toast
ingredients: 4 thick slices day-old Italian bread (or bread of choice)
1/2 teaspoon cinnamon, plus extra for serving
steps: In a medium bowl, whisk the eggs, milk, vanilla and spices. Add the bread and move the slices around gently so they soak up the mixture evenly.
Put the oats in a shallow dish.
Melt the butter over medium heat in a large nonstick pan.
Coat the soaked bread slices on both sides with the oats.
Fry over medium-high heat until golden brown on both sides.
Serve with extra cinnamon, fresh berries and plenty of maple syrup.
notes: Serves 2, about 10 minutes. Slightly crunchy, sweet and spicy. Reviewers made it with oatmeal bread and with a non-dairy milk.

title: One Pan Chicken and Potatoes
ingredients: 8 chicken thighs and drumsticks, about 2 1/2 pounds
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Dry the chicken and potatoes well with a paper towel and place in a 9x13 rimmed baking dish.
Whisk together the olive oil, lemon juice, garlic, 7 spice, paprika, salt and pepper. Drizzle over the chicken, add the potatoes, and use your hands to coat everything.
Bake uncovered 55 to 65 minutes, until the potatoes are fork tender and the chicken is cooked through. Broil 3 to 5 minutes more for color if needed.
Rest the chicken 5 minutes, then garnish with parsley.
notes: Serves 4. Leftovers keep up to 4 days. Chicken freezes well but the potatoes do not. If the potatoes aren't done when the chicken is, quarter them next time. Don't have 7 spice? Swap in Italian seasoning, Cajun or lemon pepper.

title: One Pot Cheesy Chicken Broccoli Rice Casserole
ingredients: 2 chicken breasts, cut into small cubes
10 ounces cream of chicken soup (1 can)
2 cups low-sodium chicken broth, plus more if needed
steps: Heat the oil in a large oven-proof skillet over medium. Cook the onion and chicken about 5 minutes, until the chicken browns a bit and is no longer pink. Season with salt and pepper.
Stir in the garlic and cook about 30 seconds.

Add the rice, cream of chicken soup and 2 cups broth. Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat, cover, and cook on medium (stirring now and then) about 15 minutes, until the rice is cooked. Add more broth if the rice needs it.
Stir in the broccoli and half the cheese and cook 2 more minutes, until the broccoli softens a little.
Sprinkle the rest of the cheese on top and put the skillet under the broiler a couple of minutes, until melted and starting to brown.
Garnish with parsley and serve.
notes: Serves 6. Prep 10 min, cook 20 min. Use long grain rice (basmati or jasmine). Needs a tight-fitting lid so the rice steams. If it gets too thick, stir in a splash of broth or milk. Rotisserie chicken works: add it with the broccoli. Leftovers keep 3 to 4 days in the fridge or 2 months frozen. The source lists the soup as 10 ounces (1 can); a standard can is often 10.5 oz, which works fine. Stove-only is fine if you skip the broiler step.

title: One Pot Chicken Lo Mein
ingredients: 1/2 pound boneless skinless chicken breast, cut into small chunks
1 pound box linguini or fettuccini, broken in half
4 medium carrots, peeled and cut into thin 3-inch strips
1 medium red bell pepper, cut into thin 3-inch strips
1 bunch green onions, white parts sliced and green parts cut into 3-inch strips
steps: Put the chicken in a large stockpot, then the pasta, then all the remaining ingredients. Cover.
Bring to a rolling boil over high heat, stir, and reduce the heat to medium-low.
Cook covered about 15 minutes, stirring occasionally, until most of the liquid is gone and the chicken is cooked through.
Remove the lid and let it rest 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Serves 6. Prep 15 min, cook 20 min. One pot, uncooked pasta. Vegetarian: use vegetable broth and skip the chicken. Whole wheat pasta works. Some readers found the vegetables went mushy and the dish a little bland, so they cut carrots and peppers thicker, or added salt and hoisin. Ramen or rice noodles are a more traditional swap. Add extra broth if you add more vegetables.

title: Oven Baked Pork Chops
ingredients: 4 bone-in pork chops, 1/2 to 3/4 inch thick
1 pound asparagus, green beans and/or carrots
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F with a rack in the center. Line a baking sheet with foil or parchment and lightly oil or spray it.
Pat the pork chops dry and season with salt and pepper.
Mix the Creole seasoning, thyme, garlic, Dijon, Worcestershire, brown sugar and oil. Coat the chops and marinate about 30 minutes, then drain and set them on the baking sheet.
Toss the potatoes (and the other vegetables) with salt, oil and Creole seasoning. Arrange them next to the chops.
Bake 18 to 22 minutes, until the thickest part of the chops reads 145°F.
If you like, broil 2 to 3 minutes to caramelize the tops. Garnish with parsley and serve.
notes: Serves 4. Prep 10 min, cook 20 min. Boneless chops of the same thickness take 15 to 19 minutes. Thicker chops need more time. If the potatoes are not done when the chops are, take the chops out and keep roasting the potatoes. Cut the potatoes small so they cook evenly. Salt and pepper amounts are not given (to taste). The single 2 tablespoons of oil is listed once and not split between the marinade and the vegetables. The recipe card's steps only mention seasoning the potatoes, but the blog text says to season the vegetables the same way, so the steps above do both.

title: Oven-Baked Pork Chops (The Kitchn)
ingredients: 4 center-cut, bone-in pork chops, 1 to 1 1/2 inches thick (about 10 oz each)
2 tsp neutral oil, such as vegetable
Optional brine: 4 garlic cloves, crushed and peeled
Optional brine: 1 tsp whole black peppercorns
steps: Optional brine: stir the warm water and 1/3 cup salt together until dissolved. Add the garlic, peppercorns and bay leaf, then submerge the chops. Cover and refrigerate 1 to 4 hours.
Heat the oven to 400°F. Take the chops out of the brine (or the package) and pat dry. Season all over with the salt, pepper and garlic powder.
Add the oil to a large heavy oven-safe skillet, swirl, and wipe out any excess with a paper towel. Heat over medium-high until just starting to smoke.
Sear the chops in a single layer until golden on the bottom, about 3 minutes. Stand them on their fatty edge and cook until the fat browns, 1 to 2 minutes.
Flip the chops to the uncooked side and move the skillet to the oven. Roast 6 to 10 minutes, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part reads at least 145°F.
Rest the chops on a plate, loosely tented with foil, for 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Serves 4. Prep 5 min, cook 15 to 20 min (plus brining time if used). Brining is optional; the source says chops brined 3 hours tasted nearly the same as unbrined. Leftovers keep 4 days in the fridge. FLAG: the saved link was the older Kitchn article (ID 194257), which now redirects to this recipe, republished Sept 2026 and revised from the older version. It may differ from what was originally saved. Not the same as the earlier 'Oven Baked Pork Chops' entry.

title: Pan Seared Halibut with Lemon Butter Sauce
ingredients: 4 halibut fillets, 6 ounces each (1 1/2 pounds total)
steps: Pat the fillets completely dry with paper towels. Season both sides with the garlic powder, paprika, salt and pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat for 2 minutes.
Add the fillets in a single layer (in batches if needed) and sear without moving for 3 to 4 minutes, until the edges are opaque.
Flip and cook 2 to 4 minutes, until cooked through. Remove and cover with foil to keep warm.
Reduce the heat to medium-low. Add the butter to the same pan and cook 2 to 3 minutes, stirring now and then, until browned and nutty-smelling.
Squeeze in the juice of both lemon halves, bring to a simmer, then reduce the heat and cook 3 to 4 minutes, stirring often, until reduced by half. It will still be thin.
Drizzle a little sauce on each plate, set the fish on top, and drizzle more sauce over it.
notes: Serves 4, about 15 to 20 minutes. Fish is done at 135 to 140°F. A non-stick pan works best. Keep the heat low for the sauce; several reviewers had it burn or split when the pan was too hot. Other white fish (cod, haddock, snapper) work too. Best fresh; leftovers keep 3 to 4 days.

title: Paprika Chicken & Spinach with White Wine Butter Thyme Sauce
ingredients: Salt and pepper (about 1/4 teaspoon each for seasoning the chicken, more to taste at the end)
2 handfuls spinach (chopped if the pieces are large)
steps: Rub the chicken evenly on both sides with the paprika and season with about 1/4 teaspoon each of salt and pepper.

Melt 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and add the chicken. Cook the first side 3 minutes until golden, flip, and turn the heat to medium or slightly lower. Cook 3 more minutes, then add the remaining butter, thyme and garlic.
Cook, stirring the thyme and garlic around, about 2 minutes, then add the wine.
Bring the wine to a gentle simmer, uncovered, and cook 20 minutes. It will reduce, so add more wine if needed. Leave the chicken in the skillet.
Add the spinach and let it wilt fully. Season with salt and pepper, check that the chicken is cooked through, and serve with a grain of your choice.
notes: Yield 2 to 4 servings. Prep 5 min, cook 30 min. Butter can be partly or fully replaced with olive oil (author did about half and half). Use fresh thyme, dried is about 1/3 the amount but changes the dish a lot. Strip the leaves off the woody stems. The sauce is thin and buttery, not creamy or thick. There is no cream in the recipe. Readers who wanted it thicker added 1/3 to 1/2 cup half and half or a cornstarch slurry. Several readers found the chicken dry or the sauce runny with a big pan, so use a pan where the wine comes partway up the chicken, and check the chicken early. Chicken stock plus a squeeze of lemon works if you want to skip the wine. Good with rice, potatoes, polenta or a green vegetable. Mushrooms are a popular add-in.

title: Parmesan Pasta with Broccoli and Mushrooms
ingredients: 10 ounces spaghetti (gluten free in the original)
Seasoned salt and pepper (homemade blend of salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder; amounts not given)
steps: Boil a large pot of water. Add the broccoli and cook 2 to 3 minutes until crisp tender. Scoop it out, drain, and set aside.
Return the water to a boil, cook the pasta al dente, reserve about 1 cup of the pasta water, then drain.

Meanwhile, heat a 12 inch skillet over medium-high heat. Melt 2 tablespoons butter and saute the mushrooms and shallot 10 to 12 minutes until golden brown and tender. Season with seasoned salt and pepper once browned.
Put the mushrooms, pasta, remaining 4 tablespoons butter and the parmesan in the pasta pot. Drizzle in some pasta water and stir until creamy, adding more as needed.
Add the broccoli and plenty of seasoned salt and pepper, stir once more, and serve.
notes: Serves 6, about 30 minutes. Spread the mushrooms out so they brown instead of steaming. The seasoned salt amounts aren't given; the source links a homemade recipe for it. Any pasta works.

title: Peach Glazed Chicken
ingredients: 4 boneless, skinless chicken breast halves (1 to 1 1/2 pounds each, as listed)
1 1/2 cups firmly packed light brown sugar
steps: Put the flour in a shallow dish and coat the chicken breasts completely.
Melt the butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Brown the chicken 2 to 3 minutes per side, then move to a platter.

Add the remaining ingredients (peaches, brown sugar, celery, onion, bell pepper, lemon juice, cayenne, salt) to the skillet and cook 4 to 5 minutes, until the peaches thaw and the sauce begins to thicken.
Return the chicken to the skillet and cook 8 to 10 minutes, until no pink remains and the sauce has thickened.
notes: Serves 4. Cook time 20 min. Serve over hot cooked rice to catch the sauce. The source lists the chicken as 4 breast halves of 1 to 1 1/2 pounds each, which is likely a typo for ounces, so size is not certain. 1 1/2 cups brown sugar is as written, a reader says you can use less. No pepper amount besides cayenne.

title: Penne Pasta in Creamy Vodka Tomato Sauce with Mushrooms
ingredients: 3/4 teaspoon salt, or more to taste
8 oz penne pasta (gluten-free brown rice penne works)
steps: In a large skillet over medium heat, saute the onion and garlic in the olive oil until the onion softens.
Off the heat, add the tomatoes (break them up if needed), vodka, crushed red pepper, basil and oregano and mix.
Bring gently to medium heat, then reduce to low and simmer covered, stirring occasionally, about 20 minutes until the sauce thickens. Add the mushrooms for the last 10 minutes.
On low heat, stir in the heavy cream and half and half. Season with 3/4 teaspoon salt or more.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta per the package, rinse in cold water and drain. Add it to the sauce and heat through on low.
Serve each plate topped with freshly grated Parmesan.
notes: Serves 4. Prep 10 min, cook 20 min. The source just says "canned tomatoes" (14 oz) without saying diced, crushed or whole. The step says to break them up if needed, so whole or diced would fit. One reader found 3/4 cup vodka too strong and the sauce runny, another said the sauce got better and the vodka mellowed when made a day ahead. Another reader sauteed the mushrooms with the onion and let the cream thicken longer. Chicken is a nice addition.

title: Penne with Sweet Summer Vegetables, Pine Nuts, and Herbs
ingredients: 2 ears corn, shucked, kernels cut off
2 large zucchini or summer squash, halved lengthwise and cut into 1/2-inch slices
4 tablespoons olive oil, divided (3 tablespoons and 1 tablespoon)
Coarse salt and black pepper, to taste
steps: Heat the oven to 450°F and set a pot of water on to boil.

Toss the tomatoes, squash, onion and garlic with 3 tablespoons olive oil and season well with salt and pepper. Keep the corn separate. Spread the vegetables (not the corn) on baking sheets and roast 35 to 40 minutes until sweet, golden and slightly caramelized, without tossing them much.
Add the corn to the pans for the last 15 minutes of roasting.
If using pine nuts, toast them gently in a large dry pan over medium heat, stirring constantly, and remove as soon as they turn golden.
Cook the pasta until tender but slightly al dente. Drain, return to the pot, and reserve a little cooking water.
Add the roasted vegetables, the remaining 1 tablespoon olive oil and a bit of the cooking water to the pasta. Toss in the basil and oregano and serve, topped with pine nuts.
notes: Serves 4. Meatless. Roast the tomatoes whole, they collapse as they cook. Onion can be a large dice or large slices. Several readers say the tomatoes release a lot of liquid, so roast them on a separate sheet so everything caramelizes instead of steaming. Readers also like a pound of pasta for a better veg to pasta ratio (the recipe uses 8 oz), goat cheese or feta, a splash of balsamic, and extra garlic. Use dry (egg-free) pasta for vegan, or gluten-free pasta for gluten-free. A few readers noted the squash and tomato sizes were not described in the original, which the author clarified in the comments.

title: Perfect Pan Roasted Chicken Thighs
ingredients: Kosher salt and freshly ground black pepper
Vegetable oil (amount not clearly given, the source lists just "1")
Optional rosemary pan sauce: fresh rosemary sprigs and whole garlic cloves (no amounts given)
Optional rosemary pan sauce: 1/2 cup chicken stock
Optional lemon thyme pan sauce: thin lemon slices and fresh thyme sprigs (no amounts given)
Optional lemon thyme pan sauce: 1/2 cup dry white wine
steps: Heat the oven to 475°F. Season the chicken with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a 12 inch cast iron or heavy nonstick skillet over high heat until hot but not smoking.

Nestle the chicken in the skillet skin side down and cook 2 minutes. Reduce the heat to medium-high and keep cooking skin side down, rearranging the thighs now and then and rotating the pan, until the fat renders and the skin is golden brown, about 12 minutes.
Move the skillet to the oven and cook 13 more minutes. Flip the chicken and cook until the skin is crisp and the meat is cooked through, about 5 minutes more.
Move to a plate and rest 5 minutes before serving.

Pan sauce (optional): for the rosemary version, tuck rosemary sprigs and whole garlic cloves between the thighs when the pan goes in the oven. After cooking, take out the chicken, spoon off some of the fat, add the chicken stock, bring to a boil, and spoon over the chicken.

For the lemon thyme version, put thin lemon slices and thyme sprigs in the pan with the chicken. After cooking, take out the chicken, spoon off some fat, add the white wine, bring to a boil, and spoon over the chicken.
notes: Makes 2 to 4 servings. FLAG: the saved Yahoo Shine link is gone. This is a 2012 copy on Just A Pinch of the same recipe name (original source listed as unknown), so it is not confirmed to match what you saved. The oil amount is missing in that copy. Another blog version of this method cooks it entirely on the stovetop (about 12 minutes skin side down, then about 5 minutes after flipping), so the oven time here is not the only way it has been written.

title: Pesto Cream Sauce
steps: Heat the cream and water in a small, heavy saucepan over medium heat until hot but not boiling.
Add the butter, pesto, garlic powder and salt. Reduce the heat and cook about 5 more minutes over low heat.
Stir in the parmesan until melted. Serve over pasta.
notes: Ready in 15 minutes. The page doesn't give a serving count or how much pasta it covers; one reader said it was enough for 4 to 5 servings of pasta, and others double it for a family of four. Use heavy cream, not half-and-half, and don't cut the butter, or the sauce stays thin. Reader tips for a runny sauce: skip the water, or add a little cornstarch slurry at the end. Shred the parmesan fresh, since pre-grated cheese won't melt in. Reheats well over low heat and thickens a bit. Sauce only, no pasta amount given. Matched by the exact link in your PDF (Food.com has several other recipes with this name).

title: Roasted Cornish Game Hens
ingredients: 6 Cornish game hens (about 1 to 1 1/2 pounds each), rinsed and dried thoroughly
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
Stir the salt, lemon pepper, dried basil and poultry seasoning together in a small bowl.
Rub the olive oil all over the hens and season each with the salt mixture.
Set the hens on a baking sheet with plenty of space between them (use 2 pans if needed).
Loosely stuff each cavity with some of the green pepper, celery and onion.
Roast about 1 hour, until an instant-read thermometer in the thickest part of the thigh reads 165°F and the juices run clear.
Tent loosely with foil and rest 10 minutes before carving or serving.
notes: Serves 6. Ready in about 1 hr 20 min. Recipe by Patrick and Gina Neely (Down Home with the Neelys). FLAG: the Food Network page itself did not come up, so this is taken from two copies that credit the Neelys and Food Network (Food.com and a local-grown recipe page). The amounts matched across both. Tips from the source: put a wire rack on the sheet pan (line the pan with foil under it for easy cleanup), do not crowd the hens or the skin will not crisp and they take longer. The vegetables in the cavity flavor the meat as it cooks. Easy to cut down for fewer hens.

title: Roasted Potatoes and Kielbasa
ingredients: 3 pounds small red potatoes, cut into 1/4-inch rings
2 tablespoons light olive oil or other high-heat oil
2 tablespoons minced fresh parsley (or 1/2 tablespoon dried)
1 pound kielbasa or other sausage, cut into 3/4-inch rings
steps: Heat the oven to 400°F and line a large baking sheet with parchment.
Cut the potatoes into rings about 1/4 inch thick (halve or quarter tiny ones). Slice the kielbasa into 3/4-inch rings.
Toss the potatoes and kielbasa with the parsley, garlic, salt and oil.
Spread on the baking sheet and bake 40 to 45 minutes, stirring halfway, until the potatoes are browned and crisp.
Garnish with more parsley and serve warm.
notes: Serves 4 as dinner. Prep 5 min, cook about 50 min. No need to peel the potatoes. If the sausage is lean, add it halfway through so it does not burn. Use a big enough pan so the potatoes crisp instead of steaming. A reader reported 40 minutes was too long in their oven, so check early. The source does not say whether kielbasa is pork or beef, so the Pork tag is an assumption (Polish kielbasa is usually pork).

title: Shepherd's Pie Potato Skins
ingredients: 250 g / 8 oz lamb or beef mince (ground meat)
1 1/2 cups frozen mixed vegetables (peas, corn, carrots) or fresh
1 cup beef stock/broth (or 1 bouillon cube dissolved in hot water)
4 large potatoes, scrubbed clean (about 400 g / 13 oz each)
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F (180°C).
Prick each potato about 6 times with a fork and microwave on high 5 minutes, turn, and microwave 5 more minutes until a knife slides in.

Cut the tops off the potatoes and scoop out the centers, leaving a thin skin (about 1/4 inch). Mash the scooped potato with the milk, butter and salt until smooth. If you want to pipe it, put the mash in a bag with a large star tip.
For the filling: heat the olive oil in a large pan over medium-high. Saute the onion and garlic 2 minutes. Turn the heat to high, add the meat and cook about 3 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.

Sprinkle over the flour and stir. Add the vegetables, stock, water, salt, thyme, oregano and pepper, bring to a simmer, and stir about 2 minutes until the sauce is thick and glossy. Take off the heat.
Fill each potato with a slightly heaped amount of filling and press it in. Pipe or spoon the mashed potato on top and fluff it with a fork (you will not use all of it).
Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the mash browns on the ridges. Serve right away.
notes: Serves 4. Prep 5 min, cook 10 min (15 total, plus baking in the oven). Meat is lamb for traditional shepherd's pie, beef makes a cottage pie. Potatoes can be baked instead of microwaved (about 40 to 50 minutes at 350°F). In a hurry, skip the bake and brown the top under the broiler, but baking lets the filling flavor develop. Freezes well, best frozen after baking, reheat about 20 minutes at 350°F. Parmesan on the mash adds crunch. Some readers found it a bit bland or the filling greyish and added Worcestershire sauce.

title: Shrimp and Mushroom Linguini with Creamy Cheese Herb Sauce
steps: Bring a large pot of lightly salted water to a boil. Cook the linguini until tender, about 7 minutes, then drain.
Meanwhile, melt 2 tbsp butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Cook and stir the mushrooms until tender, then move them to a plate.
In the same pan, melt 1/2 cup butter with the garlic. Add the cream cheese and break it up with a spoon as it melts.
Stir in the parsley and basil and simmer for 5 minutes.
Mix in the boiling water until the sauce is smooth. Stir in the cooked shrimp and mushrooms and heat through.
Toss the linguini with the sauce and serve.
notes: Serves 4. Ready in about 15 minutes. FLAG: the saved MSN link could not be opened. This matches the Allrecipes recipe of the same name, as reposted on Food.com; the amounts come from a copy of the Allrecipes version on Just A Pinch, and the steps from the Food.com page. Not confirmed to be the exact copy you saved. Shrimp is pre-cooked; reviewers often used a full pound. Reader tip: if the sauce comes out soupy, let it sit on the pasta for 3 to 5 minutes. Source gives no salt amount.

title: Smoked Beef and Cheese Sliders
ingredients: Garlic (powder, salt, fresh, frozen, or minced)
steps: Cut chuck roast into large chunks.
Coat with mustard as a binder, then season with salt, pepper, garlic powder, and all-purpose seasoning.
Sear on the stove.
Crockpot with 1/2 cup beef stock: 5-6 hrs on high or 8-10 on low. Re-add seasonings.
Last 1/2 hr, add butter and brown sugar to each chunk.
Shred with some of the juice.
Toast the middles of the buns in the air fryer, middle side up.
Melt 5 tbsp butter with garlic. Brush half on the bottom layer of buns.
Layer provolone, meat, BBQ drizzle, then frizzled onions.
Bake at 350°F for 15 min.
notes: Air fryer toasting: on 4 slices, 3 dark.

title: Smothered Chicken with Mushroom Gravy
ingredients: Salt and pepper, for the chicken
1 shallot, minced (or 1/4 cup finely minced yellow or white onion)
8 oz white button or baby bella mushrooms, chopped
1 1/2 cups low-sodium chicken or beef broth
steps: Season both sides of the chicken with salt and pepper. Heat the olive oil in a 12-inch nonstick skillet over medium heat until hot. Cook the chicken about 4 minutes per side, until golden and cooked through (165°F). Move to a plate and cover to keep warm.

Melt the butter in the same pan over medium heat. Add the shallot, mushrooms, 1/4 tsp salt, thyme and garlic. Cook, stirring often, 8 to 10 minutes, until the mushrooms are tender and golden and most of the liquid has evaporated.
Sprinkle the flour over the mushrooms and stir for 1 to 2 minutes.
Slowly whisk in the broth, a little at a time, whisking until thick before adding more, so the flour doesn't clump.
Stir in the milk and simmer 5 to 7 minutes, until thick and bubbly. Season with salt and pepper.
Spoon the gravy over the chicken and serve, ideally with mashed potatoes.
notes: Serves 4. Prep 15 min, cook about 22 min. No amount given for the salt and pepper on the chicken or to taste. Tip from the source: if the breasts are thick, cut them in half into thinner cutlets (4 to 6 pieces total). Don't overcook the chicken.

title: Spaghetti Alla Primavera
ingredients: 1 small zucchini, quartered lengthwise, cut into 1-inch lengths, blanched
Kosher salt and pepper, to taste
steps: Blanch the asparagus, broccoli, peas and zucchini ahead of time, and cook the spaghetti al dente.
Heat 5 tablespoons of the oil in a 12-inch skillet over medium. Add two thirds of the garlic and cook until golden, about 2 minutes. Add the mushrooms and cook until golden, about 3 minutes.
Add the asparagus, broccoli, peas and zucchini and cook 3 minutes.
Add the pasta, cream, Parmesan and butter, season with salt and pepper, toss to combine, and transfer to a platter.
Bring the remaining oil and garlic, the tomatoes and the basil to a simmer over medium heat. Pour over the pasta and garnish with pine nuts.
notes: Serves 4 to 6. The recipe is Sirio Maccioni's from Le Cirque (Saveur). The source says the vegetables are "blanched" but gives no times, so cook each until just crisp-tender. Salt and pepper have no amount. The saved link redirects to saveur.com/article/Recipes/Classic-Spaghetti-Primavera/.

title: Spaghetti with Shrimp in a Creamy Tomato Sauce
ingredients: 1 lb medium raw shrimp, peeled and deveined
3/4 lb spaghetti or angel hair pasta
2 tbsp olive oil, for cooking the shrimp
1 tbsp olive oil, for the pasta water
1 small onion, or 1/4 cup green onion, finely chopped
