1/2 tsp dried basil, or 2 tbsp chopped fresh basil
steps: Pat the shrimp dry on paper towels. Season lightly with salt and pepper and saute in 2 tbsp olive oil over medium-high heat until just cooked through, about 3 minutes, flipping halfway. Set aside.

Put the tomatoes, onion, chili flakes, basil, garlic and butter in a heavy pan and season with salt and pepper. Add the wine and cook over medium-high heat until the mixture is soft and most of the wine has evaporated, leaving about 1/4 cup liquid.
Meanwhile, cook the pasta in salted water with 1 tbsp olive oil until al dente. Rinse, drain and set aside.
When the sauce has mostly evaporated, stir in the cream and add the shrimp. Warm through gently for 2 minutes and season to taste.
Toss the pasta with the sauce, sprinkle with Parmesan and serve.
notes: Serves 6. Prep 15 min, cook 15 min. The source's ingredient list gives 1 tbsp olive oil, but the steps use 2 tbsp for the shrimp plus 1 tbsp in the pasta water, so this entry follows the steps. No amount given for the salt and pepper or the Parmesan.

title: Stove Top Beef Stew
ingredients: 1 teaspoon dried rosemary, crushed between your fingers
1 large shallot or small onion, finely chopped
1 1/2 pounds stew meat, cut into 1/2 inch pieces
steps: Heat the oil in a large Dutch oven over medium heat. Add the thyme and rosemary and cook 30 seconds.
Add the carrots, celery and shallot, season with salt and pepper, and saute about 10 minutes until browned and tender.
Add the mushrooms and saute 7 to 9 minutes, until their liquid cooks off. Add the garlic and cook 1 minute.
Turn the heat to medium-high, add the stew meat, red pepper flakes and more salt and pepper, and saute 8 to 10 minutes until browned.
Mash the butter and flour together with a fork, stir it into the pot, and cook 1 minute.
Stream in the beef broth, scraping up the browned bits. Bring to a simmer on high, add the bay leaves, cover, turn to low, and simmer 2 hours, stirring occasionally.
Remove the lid and simmer gently another 1 1/2 hours, until the meat is tender and the stew is thick. Put the lid back on if it reduces too fast.
Adjust the salt and pepper, add the peas, and simmer 2 minutes. Remove the bay leaves and serve over mashed potatoes.
notes: Serves 6, about 4 hours. Chop the vegetables very fine so they melt into the gravy. Freezes well; thaw in the fridge and reheat on the stove.

title: The Best Swedish Meatballs
ingredients: 2 cups beef broth (low sodium works well)
steps: Mix the beef, panko, parsley, allspice, nutmeg, onion, garlic powder, pepper, salt and egg until combined.
Roll into 12 large or 20 small meatballs.
Heat the olive oil and 1 tablespoon butter in a large skillet over medium-high. Cook the meatballs 7 to 8 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through. Move to a plate and cover with foil.
Add 4 tablespoons butter and the flour to the same skillet and whisk until it turns brown.
Slowly whisk in the beef broth and cream, then add the Worcestershire and Dijon. Simmer until the sauce thickens, and season with salt and pepper.
Return the meatballs to the skillet and simmer 1 to 2 minutes. Serve over egg noodles or mashed potatoes.
notes: Serves 6. Prep 10 min, cook 20 min. No panko: blend 2 slices of bread to crumbs and mix with 1/4 cup milk. To skip pan-searing, broil the meatballs on a sprayed sheet pan 5 to 7 minutes, flip, then 4 to 5 more minutes, and pour the drippings into the sauce pan. Cooked meatballs freeze up to 3 months. Do not freeze the cream sauce, it separates.

title: TN Pasta
ingredients: 1 large sweet onion, sliced into rings and halved
2 bell peppers (1 orange and 1 red), sliced
A couple cloves of garlic, chopped
Olive oil (amount not given, "a decent amount" for cooking the vegetables, plus a little more at the end if needed)
steps: Boil water for the penne.
Cook the sausage. Place it on a plate and don't rinse out the pan.
Slice the onion into rings, then cut the rings in half. Slice the orange and red bell peppers. Chop the garlic.
In the same pan, cook the onions and peppers in a decent amount of olive oil for about 5 minutes.
Add the garlic.
Leave everything in the pan, add the cooked penne and the sausage, and sprinkle with a little more olive oil if needed.
notes: Source and serving size not given.

title: Twice Baked Sweet Potatoes with Walnut Streusel
steps: Heat the oven to 350°F. Prick the sweet potatoes with a fork and bake about 30 minutes, until soft. Microwaving on high 13 to 15 minutes also works.
Slice the cooked potatoes in half and scoop the centers into a bowl, leaving a 1/4 inch border with the skin.
Mix the brown sugar, butter, salt and cinnamon into the scooped sweet potato until smooth. Spoon the filling back into the shells.
In a small bowl, mix the streusel ingredients until the butter starts to warm and everything sticks together.
Top the filled potatoes with the streusel and bake 20 to 30 minutes. Serve warm.
notes: Serves 6. FLAG: the saved cookitfresh page (2012) did not open. This copy, from the Atlanta Jewish Times (credited to What2Cook), has the same title and matches another blog copy, so it is very likely the same recipe but not confirmed. A Just A Pinch copy differs a bit: 45 minute first bake, 1/2 teaspoon each of salt and cinnamon in the filling, 1/2 teaspoon cinnamon in the streusel, melted butter, and 25 more minutes in the oven. The butter in the streusel isn't described as cold or melted here.

title: Unstuffed Pepper Casserole
ingredients: 2 medium red, yellow or green bell peppers, cut into 3/4-inch pieces (about 2 cups)
1 can (14.5 oz) diced tomatoes with Italian herbs
1 bag (10 oz) frozen cooked white rice
2 cups shredded Cheddar cheese (8 oz), divided
steps: Heat the oven to 375°F.
In a 12-inch skillet over medium-high, cook the sausage, peppers, onion and garlic 8 to 10 minutes, stirring now and then, until the sausage is no longer pink. Drain.
Return the mixture to the skillet and stir in the tomatoes, rice and 1 cup of the cheese.
Pour into an ungreased 13x9-inch (3-quart) glass baking dish and cover with foil.
Bake 15 to 20 minutes, until the cheese is melted.
Uncover, sprinkle with the remaining 1 cup cheese, and bake uncovered 4 to 6 minutes more, until melted.
notes: Serves 6. Prep 20 min, total 40 min. Use sweet Italian sausage for a milder dish. The original calls for Muir Glen organic diced tomatoes with Italian herbs, but any can of that size works. No salt or pepper in the source.

title: Air Fryer Brats
steps: Thaw the brats before cooking.
Preheat the air fryer to 390°F.
Arrange the sausages in a single layer in the air fryer basket.
Cook for 10–11 minutes, turning once halfway through, until browned and the internal temperature is 160°F.
notes: Method from the Johnsonville beer brat package.

title: Curried Chicken Salad
steps: If not using shredded chicken from another recipe, preheat the oven to 350°F.
Place the chicken breasts on a sheet pan sprayed with oil or cooking spray and sprinkle liberally with salt and pepper.
Bake 18-20 minutes, until cooked through (165°F) and no longer pink. Set aside until cool enough to handle, then cut into bite-sized pieces.
In a medium bowl, combine 1/3 cup of the mayonnaise, the chutney, curry powder, and a dash of salt. Whisk until smooth.
Combine first with just the chicken. If it's a little dry, add more mayo, one tablespoon at a time.
Add the celery, green onions, raisins, and cashews and mix until just combined.
Serve over salad greens or as a sandwich. Best served cold.

title: Lazy Lasagna Casserole
ingredients: 10 ounces campanelle (or penne, ziti, or medium shells)
1 teaspoon dried parsley flakes (or 1 tablespoon fresh)
steps: Cook the pasta one minute shy of the package directions. Drain well and set aside.
In a large, deep skillet or Dutch oven, cook the beef, onion, and ½ teaspoon of the garlic over medium heat until no pink remains. Drain the grease and return the pan to the heat.

Add the Italian seasoning, salt, and ¼ teaspoon of the pepper and cook, stirring, for a minute or two. Add the marinara and water and simmer a couple of minutes until warmed through. Stir in the pasta and remove from the heat.
Preheat the oven to 350°F and coat a 13x9-inch baking dish with cooking spray.
Stir the ricotta and egg together until smooth. Mix in half the mozzarella, the remaining garlic, half the Parmesan, the parsley, and the remaining pepper.
Spread half the beef and pasta mixture in the dish. Spoon dollops of the ricotta mixture over the top, then cover with the remaining beef and pasta mixture.
Cover with foil and bake 30 minutes. Remove the foil, sprinkle with the remaining mozzarella and Parmesan, and bake uncovered 5 to 10 minutes more, until bubbly.
Garnish with fresh basil and let stand 5 minutes before serving.
notes: Serves 6. About 50 minutes total. To freeze: assemble through the final beef and pasta layer, wrap tightly in heavy-duty foil, and freeze unbaked. Thaw overnight in the fridge, let sit out 30 minutes, add the final cheeses, and bake (longer if still cold).

title: Meatball Appetizers
ingredients: 2 pounds ground beef or pork (as meatballs)
steps: Brown the meatballs.
Mix the sauce ingredients over medium heat until the sugar is melted.
Simmer the meatballs in the sauce for 30 minutes.
For a crock pot, cook on high for about 3 hours, then switch to low.
notes: Make 3 batches of the sauce for 1 bag of Sam's Club meatballs (6 lbs). May use ready-made meatballs from Sam's Club or mini hot dogs.

title: Muffin Tin Meatloaf
ingredients: 1.5 lbs hamburger (93/7 so it's less greasy)
A few shakes of garlic powder
Sauce: 1.5 Tbs brown sugar (maybe a bit more)
steps: Preheat the oven to 375°F.
Mix the hamburger, egg, breadcrumbs, onion, milk, garlic powder, salt, and pepper.
Fill the muffin tin cups right to the top. Make a small divot in each with a spoon for the sauce. There may be a bit of mix left over.
Mix the catsup, Worcestershire, and brown sugar until the sugar dissolves, then spoon onto each muffin.
Bake uncovered at 375°F for about 25-30 minutes, until a meat thermometer reads 165°F.
notes: Sauce amounts are the author's best guess (not usually measured).

title: One-Pot Creamy Tomato Tortellini Soup
ingredients: 1 sprig fresh rosemary, chopped (or ½ teaspoon dried)
4 large fresh basil leaves (or ½ teaspoon dried basil)
½ cup shredded Parmesan, plus extra for garnish
steps: In a 6-quart soup pot or Dutch oven, sauté the onion, garlic, olive oil, and fresh rosemary over medium heat for 5 minutes, or until the onion is translucent.
Add the diced tomatoes, tomato sauce, oregano, basil, salt, pepper, chicken stock, and heavy cream and stir to combine. Simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the tortellini and cook 12-15 minutes, or until tender and cooked through.
Serve garnished with fresh basil and shredded Parmesan.
notes: Serves 8. Prep 10 min, cook 37 min (47 min total). By Chelsea at Gal on a Mission.

title: Shepherd's Pie
ingredients: 1 pound chicken or turkey, cooked and cut into chunks
steps: Sauté the onion and celery in 1 Tbsp butter.
Microwave the vegetables until thawed and partially cooked.
Stir the cream of chicken soup, spices, and vegetables into the onion and celery.
Gently add the meat and stir.
Place in a casserole and spread the mashed potatoes over the top.
Drizzle with butter.
Bake at 375°F for 30-45 minutes.
notes: Serves 4. A great meal in one casserole.

title: Sloppy Joes
steps: Brown the meat, add the onions, and simmer until tender.
Add the other ingredients and simmer for at least 30 minutes.

title: Stuffed Pepper Soup
steps: In a large stock pot, brown the ground meat. Drain the fat, then add the pepper and onion and cook until the onion is translucent, not letting it brown.
Add the tomatoes, tomato sauce, broth, thyme, and sage and season with salt and pepper. Cover and simmer 30-45 minutes, until the peppers are tender.
In another saucepan, boil 2 cups of water, add the rice, and cook until tender. Add the rice to the soup, heat through, and serve.
notes: Serves 6. Recipe from Michelle Lambert Webb.

title: Bagel Pizzas
ingredients: ¼ cup Kroger frozen chopped onions
steps: Preheat the oven to 400°F. Line a baking sheet with foil for easy cleanup.
Spread the frozen chopped onions in a single layer on a paper towel and pat dry (excess moisture makes the bagels soggy). Let them sit while you prep.
Place the bagel halves cut-side up on the baking sheet and toast in the oven for 4–5 minutes, until lightly crisped. This keeps them from getting soggy under the sauce.
Spread about 1–1.5 tablespoons of Rao's sauce on each half, leaving a small border at the edge. Don't overdo it or it'll be wet.
Divide the shredded cheese evenly over the halves. Top each with about 4 pepperoni and a pinch of the dried onions.
Bake at 400°F for 8–10 minutes, until the cheese is melted and bubbly and the pepperoni cups are crisped at the edges.
Optional: broil for the last 1–2 minutes for extra browning. Watch closely, it goes from perfect to burnt fast.
Let rest 2 minutes before eating, since the cheese and sauce hold a lot of heat. Slice if desired, or eat whole.
notes: Serves 4. Classic homemade bagel pizzas with crispy edges and melty cheese. Tips: pre-toasting the bagels is the #1 trick for avoiding sogginess. Cup n' Crisp pepperoni curls up and crisps, and the little grease cups are great. Rao's sauce is thicker than most jarred sauces, so it won't run. Whole wheat bagels are denser and hold up well. The frozen onions don't need to cook through; just pat them dry and they soften in the oven.
